title: Why Nobody Has A Landline Anymore
hook: Your landline is dying: 1.26 billion lines in 2006, just 815 million now.
closing: The phone didn't die. It just stopped ringing at home.
question: Do you even own a landline anymore?

segments.say: Fixed telephone lines peaked at 1.26 billion in 2006, then started falling fast.
What replaced them wasn't a phone -- broadband subscriptions exploded sevenfold since 2005, to 1.65 billion.
China alone now runs 670 million of those broadband lines -- more than the next four countries combined.
